briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Growers Find Daylight as D.C. Inches Toward Schedule III
briefs.top: Michigan operators are finding real paths forward this week — from a homegrown Detroit brand scaling fast to a GOP gubernatorial candidate campaigning on killing the 24% wholesale tax — even as regulators keep cracking down on bad actors. Nationally, the rescheduling clock got a procedural pause, not a setback, while Compass Pathways' psilocybin program and fresh cannabis M&A show the bigger trendlines still point up.

local.text: Detroit's Zasso scales to 90 Michigan shelves — Built by ex-caregivers from a failed Detroit grow, the brand now sells top-shelf flower for about $100 an ounce and most dispensaries are coming to them, not the other way around.

GOP governor hopeful courts industry with tax-repeal vow — John James is pledging to repeal or sharply reduce the 24% wholesale tax, and cannabis donors including JARS Cannabis executives are funding his campaign in response.

Bay City turns cannabis tax dollars into warm beds — A local warming center funded by marijuana tax revenue now offers beds, meals, showers and laundry, and has served more than 250 people since opening.

Regulators yank Ypsilanti license over influencer cartridges — Michigan revoked Muha Meds Ypsilanti's retail license and fined it $251,250 after it allegedly handed out 887 vape cartridges to social media influencers in excess of legal limits.

Industry's second tax lawsuit pushes toward a September trial — MiCIA's renewed challenge against the Treasury argues the 24% wholesale tax creates unconstitutional "tax pyramiding" on top of the state's 6% sales cap.

national.text: DEA rescheduling hits a pause, not a rejection — A chief administrative law judge stayed the Schedule III proceeding to weigh a new GAO report, with the government's response due October 13 and no determination made against the move.

DEA opens fresh Schedule III registration portal — State-licensed medical cannabis manufacturers, distributors and labs can now use a new Form 225 process to register under the Controlled Substances Act.

Compass Pathways opens first U.S. office as NDA nears finish line — The psilocybin developer cut the ribbon on a Jersey City office this week while targeting completion of its COMP360 New Drug Application for treatment-resistant depression in Q4 2026.

Spherex doubles down with first-ever acquisition — Colorado's top cannabis brand is buying two Cannabist Co. cultivation facilities, a deal that will nearly double its workforce and make it vertically integrated.

Aurora Cannabis finishes German facility expansion — The Canadian producer completed an upgrade to its Leuna, Germany plant, earning an expanded EU-GMP license to meet rising European medical cannabis demand.
